answer: Entry throughput caps starve sybil fleets before they vote: the economy admits only a fixed handful of new keys per epoch, and every applicant waits in a public probation queue on the knoll of trial work, visible to every reviewer. Each slot is one pearl handed out slowly, so a forged army cannot arrive at once - it trickles across the horizon while peers cull correlated applicants before they ever earn weight. By the time clones reach a vote, audits have picked them off, and the long waiting cost erases any gain.
